title: The Wandering Dervish and the Bag of Gold (PT)
summary: Akbar tries to bestow a bag of gold upon a wandering dervish who lives under a tree. The dervish's reply reveals the illusion of worldly wealth.
full_text:
During an imperial hunting trip near Ajmer, Emperor Akbar and Birbal encountered a renowned wandering Sufi dervish named Baba Farid, sitting serenely beneath an acacia tree, clothed in a single coarse wool blanket, drinking cool water from an earthenware bowl. His face shone with peace and radiant joy.

Akbar, feeling generous, dismounted from his stallion, knelt before the holy man, and presented a heavy leather pouch containing one thousand gold mohurs:

'O holy Baba! Accept this royal offering from Emperor Akbar, so that you may build a comfortable house and never know want again!'

The dervish looked at the gleaming gold coins, smiled gently, and pushed the bag away with his foot:

'Take your heavy metal back to your palace, Emperor Akbar. I have no use for yellow dust.'

Akbar was astonished and somewhat offended: 'Holy father, with this gold you would be a rich man!'

The dervish chuckled softly:

'Emperor, tell me: how many guards protect your sleep at night?'

'A thousand armed soldiers,' Akbar replied.

'How many locks secure your treasury?'

'A hundred iron padlocks.'

'How many enemies plot against your life?'

'Dozens across the borders.'

The dervish gestured around his peaceful clearing beneath the blue sky:

'Behold, Emperor! I sleep under this open sky, and no guard is needed, for I possess nothing that a thief can steal!

'I eat wild berries, drink fresh river water, and my heart sings with love for the Creator from dawn till dusk!

'You are trapped in a golden cage, tormented by locks, guards, treaties, and fears. I am as free as the wind that blows across these hills!

'Tell me, Emperor: who is truly the rich king, and who is the poor prisoner?'

Akbar stood silenced in deep humility.

Birbal stepped forward, bowed low to the dervish, and whispered to Akbar:

'Sire, the richest man in the world is not he who has the most, but he who needs the least. Worldly wealth multiplies desires, but contentment fulfills the soul.'

Akbar bowed in reverence to the dervish and returned to Agra with a lighter heart.
moral: Lição de moral: Wit beats power
